question: Should OpenClaw accept Telegram group/topic UI config overrides and the cron no-delivery wake suppression together in this PR after metadata and proof are fixed, or should the cron behavior be split?
rationale: The PR adds new user-facing config surface and changes cron wake/message semantics, so maintainers should confirm the product boundary instead of letting proof or CI alone decide the combined scope.

options.title: Require refresh and proof first
options.body: Keep the combined PR only if it is rebased, generated metadata is refreshed, and redacted proof covers both Telegram scoped UI behavior and cron no-delivery wake suppression.

options.title: Split cron behavior
options.body: Accept the Telegram scoped UI design separately and move cron no-delivery wake semantics into a dedicated PR with its own proof.

options.title: Replace stale branch
options.body: If the contributor cannot refresh the conflicting branch, close or replace it with a narrow current-main implementation that preserves the useful Telegram design.

recommendation.title: Require refresh and proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the combined PR only if it is rebased, generated metadata is refreshed, and redacted proof covers both Telegram scoped UI behavior and cron no-delivery wake suppression.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses plugin/config metadata architecture and Telegram channel boundaries where steipete has recent adjacent ownership history.
